blocks.content: kubectl uncordon reverses a cordon, making a node schedulable again, the natural closing step of a maintenance workflow.
uncordon does exactly one thing, it undoes the unschedulable flag set by cordon, covered in the previous topic, nothing more complex than that.

blocks.alt: A direct, simple reversal of the previous topic's action

blocks.content: Once uncordoned, the scheduler once again considers this node a valid candidate for new Pods, exactly as it would any other healthy, ready node in the cluster.

blocks.alt: Fully eligible again, exactly like any other healthy node in the cluster

blocks.content: Put together with the previous two topics, this completes a genuinely standard operational sequence: cordon (stop new work landing there), drain (safely move existing work off), perform the actual maintenance, then uncordon (bring it back into active service).

blocks.alt: The complete, standard sequence, from start to finish

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: kubectl uncordon reverses cordon, making a node fully schedulable again, exactly like any other healthy node.
Together with cordon and drain, it completes the standard node maintenance workflow: cordon, drain, maintain, then uncordon.
